Primary bug is FIXED — .demo-dark class pins CSS vars to dark values with the demo section rendering bg=rgb(10,10,10) with text=rgb(250,250,250) (active) and rgb(161,161,161) (inactive) even when the page theme is light. All landing composition elements present: hero headline 'knows your business.' (1x), eyebrow 'A PLUG-AND-PLAY OPERATING SYSTEM' (visible), Register now (3x), Learn more (1x), [data-testid=plugin-ready-tag] (1x), Number labels (Install, Data leaks, Cache hit, Auto docs), pillars (Contextual/Scoped/Plug-and-play), demo header 'Not a screenshot.', closer 'Your CRM is loud.', all nav links (How, Tech Stack, Pricing, About, Contact, API Docs, FAQ, Sign in). Admin login → /app dashboard renders, Ask/OS FAB visible (chat backend already validated by test_chat_admin_basic returning valid answer with Northwind/task-01).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Landing has been fully rewritten (Apple composition). Demo & ProductMoment containers wrapped in .demo-dark and now render dark in both themes. Contrast values captured: bg rgb(10,10,10), active-step text rgb(250,250,250), inactive text rgb(161,161,161) — both well above WCAG AA. backend_test.py continues to cover contact, waitlist, chat basic, chat 429 quota, and monthly reset. Only outstanding light-theme contrast concern (from iter 2) worth spot-checking on new nav/CTA is not observable now that hero uses text-primary + solid Register CTA and secondary Learn more still uses bordered button — both visible in light mode screenshot.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: In light mode, narration/product panels inside the demo section inherited the light theme's foreground vars (dark text) but their parent card backgrounds were still dark, causing near-invisible dark-on-dark or light-on-light text as content flowed. Fix: A new .demo-dark utility in index.css re-declares --background, --foreground, --card, --card-foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --border etc. back to dark palette values inside that subtree, forcing the demo island to render as if data-theme='dark' regardless of the page theme. Verified computed styles inside .demo-dark: bg rgb(10,10,10) with foreground rgb(250,250,250) even when documentElement data-theme='light'.
